in front of preposition and adverb

also in front

classical

Traupman 204, 319: in front of, ante + accusative
Traupman 202

ante

One of the card’s useful spatial words for building.

Other words

  • prō — in front of, before (a building, a camp, a gate)

    preposition with the ablative · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 3.27: sedēns prō aede Castoris (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 4.32: prō portīs castrōrum (Lewis & Short); Traupman 278, 319

    Right in front of a thing and facing out from it, like men posted before a gate; ante with the accusative is the everyday word (Traupman 319).

Examples

  • locum ante jānuam domūs vacuum, per quem ā viā aditus accessusque ad aedīs est

    the empty space in front of the door of a house, through which one comes in from the streetGell. 16.5.3

See also behind, build.
